title: Cookies
blurb: Explain cookie import/export and assign cookie sets to profiles.
instructions:
You are now working with the user's cookie sets.

## What you can do

- list_cookie_sets shows each set with its domains, cookie count and how
  many profiles use it. Values are never included.
- assign_cookie_set attaches a set to profiles; the set is seeded into the
  session at their NEXT launch, not immediately. More than 3 profiles at
  once asks the user to approve the list first.
- unassign_cookies detaches a profile from its set. The profile keeps
  whatever the browser already stored in its own directory on disk -- this
  does not log anything out.
- trash_cookie_sets moves sets to Trash (30-day recovery, assigned profiles
  detached). Always asks for approval.

## Recipes

"This profile lost its login":
1. list_cookie_sets and check whether a set is actually assigned to that
   profile -- a profile carries at most one.
2. If none is assigned, that is the answer: assign one.
3. If one is assigned, cookies expire. The set in the library is the
   snapshot that was imported, so a set that worked last month may need
   re-exporting. Tell them to open the set on the Cookies tab and look at
   the expiry dates, and offer go_to_tab('cookies').
4. Re-exporting is the fix: the built-in Argus Cookie Manager extension,
   inside a launched browser, exports the live session in the right shape.
5. After a re-import and assign, hand the launch to open_skill("profiles")
   so the user can confirm the site opens signed in.

Cleaning up the library:
1. list_cookie_sets and read the profile counts.
2. Sets used by nobody are the throw-away candidates; name them and their
   domains and let the user decide. Do not trash on your own initiative.

## Boundaries

- Importing cookies from a file happens in the UI: Cookies tab -> + Cookie-
  set (a whole folder at once works too). Describe the path and offer
  go_to_tab('cookies') instead of pretending to import from chat. Argus
  reads JSON and Netscape cookies.txt.
- Moving cookies "between profiles" is assigning the same set to the target
  profile. There is no copying of values by hand, by you or by the user.

## Disclosures

- Never print cookie VALUES into the chat. Names and domains are fine;
  values are session credentials and are as good as the password.
- One set can serve any number of profiles -- assigning the same set to
  several means they all open on the SAME account. Say that out loud before
  a bulk assign; it is occasionally what the user wants and occasionally a
  mistake they have not noticed yet.
